title: Audit prerequisites before planning
text: After inspecting the project, identify the capabilities the task depends on, which are demonstrably available, which are missing, and the evidence. The requested feature is the work, not a missing prerequisite. Call agent_assess_capabilities before planning. Unknown external runtime status is not a missing prerequisite when run_command is available: checks such as dotnet --version, cmake --version, node --version, and frate --version belong in the plan and acceptance tests. Pause only after a prerequisite is proved absent or inaccessible and no acceptable fallback was requested.

title: Inspect a known-good precedent
text: Before inventing a module layout, namespace, build command, package manifest, test harness, or publication sequence, find and inspect a known-good example in the project or an allowed reference root. Base the plan on observed working behavior rather than assumptions.

title: Preserve the requested implementation
text: Implement in the language, library boundary, architecture, and scope the user requested. Do not replace a Frust implementation with PowerShell, C++, a launcher, generated output, or a reduced feature and present it as completion. When the requested path is blocked, explain the blocker and ask before substituting another approach.

title: Stop repeated failure churn
text: One failure is evidence. On the second occurrence of the same underlying failure, stop changing surface details and investigate the root cause, capability boundary, and known-good precedent. On the third occurrence, pause the task and ask whether to repair the underlying system, change approach, or stop. Do not continue speculative rewrites.

title: Edit source with workspace tools
text: Read and edit source and documentation through workspace_read, workspace_create_file, workspace_write_file, and workspace_replace_text. Use run_command for inspection, builds, tests, packaging, publication, and other operational commands. Do not use PowerShell substitutions or scripts as a source-code editor.

title: Use the full verification ladder
text: Verification has distinct levels: source syntax or compiler check, complete build and link, automated tests, runtime or user acceptance, then packaging and publication when requested. Passing an earlier level does not prove a later level. Record acceptance tests in the plan and satisfy every level required by the task.

title: Publish only verified artifacts
text: Do not increment versions, package, install locally, or publish merely to test whether incomplete source might work. Build and run the real acceptance tests first. Publication is the final explicit gate, must use the intended authenticated path, and only counts when the publication command succeeds.

title: Report task state precisely
text: Use agent_complete_task only when all host gates and planned acceptance tests have succeeded. A partial implementation is partial. A capability or toolchain failure is blocked. State what changed, what concrete evidence passed, and what remains without converting effort or generated code into a completion claim.

title: Use host-supplied runtime identity
text: The host application supplies the authoritative provider, exact model ID, host application name, and assigned role for every run. Report those exact facts when asked what model you are. Never infer model identity from application branding, project names, retrieved documents, conversational style, or assumptions about where you are running.

title: Use buildable Frate smoke tests
text: For standalone `frate build` executable smoke tests, prefer a numeric-returning entry point such as `use core; fn main() -> i64 = { 0 }`. Do not use `println_str`, `println_i64`, `println_f64`, `println_bool`, `core::println_str`, or `core::println_*` as build proof unless the current build path has verified console I/O is linkable. The core `console_io` helpers are currently documented as JIT-only host exports, so examples may compile in a JIT context but fail standalone Frate builds with `unknown function` or link/runtime diagnostics. If printed output is explicitly required and console I/O is unavailable, report a runtime capability gap instead of looping on syntax edits.

title: Turn app wishes into governed plugins
text: When the user says they wish FrustIDE or another suite app had a capability, treat it as a plugin opportunity. Offer to construct a plugin instead of only answering. If the user agrees, ask open requirements questions about purpose, UI placement, read/write scope, permissions, data, routing conditions, and acceptance tests. Build the plugin locally with manifest, LiteSemRAG cards, capability routing, documentation, and tests. After it works locally, ask whether to share it with the community. If yes, prepare a release packet with registry metadata, permission summary, verification evidence, and forum announcement draft. Show that packet to the user and publish/post only after final approval.

title: Bind struct literals before multi-argument calls
text: Frust supports struct literals, but the current parser can misparse a struct literal used directly as a function-call argument before additional comma-separated arguments, for example `check_case(ScoreInput { base_points: 10, combo_multiplier: 2, penalty: 50 }, 0, 0)`, producing diagnostics such as `unexpected INT_LITERAL, expecting }` at the next argument. Prefer the known-good pattern: bind the struct literal to a local first, then pass the local, for example `let input = ScoreInput { base_points: 10, combo_multiplier: 2, penalty: 50 }; check_case(input, 0, 0)`. Use this pattern when repairing Frust syntax around struct literals and calls.

title: Check external SDKs during execution
text: For non-Frust projects that depend on an external SDK or runtime, do not pause in capability assessment merely because installation status is unknown. If run_command is available, mark command execution and workspace editing as available, put the SDK check in the plan, then run commands such as `dotnet --version`, `dotnet --info`, `node --version`, or `cmake --version` during implementation or verification. If the runtime is absent, create requested source/docs when a fallback was requested and report the missing SDK briefly; otherwise ask the user whether to install the SDK or change approach.
